A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same canopy-height mapping work. Their text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix material.

before.justification: V1 reports original training experiments, GEDI-based evaluations of canopy-height predictions, model-configuration comparisons, and temporal mapping results in Section 4.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds spectral-band and seasonal ablations, forest-type evaluations, activation visualizations, and potential-deforestation area estimates in Appendices B and C.

M1.justification: The proposed 3D U-Net, monthly Sentinel-2 inputs, repeated Sentinel-1 composite, modified Huber loss with track shifts, and spline post-processing are retained. The appendix tests input variants without adopting them as changes to the final method.

E1.justification: Appendix B.2.2 newly uses the Copernicus Forest Type Map (2018) to supply broadleaf/coniferous annotations for evaluation. This is an auxiliary data addition; the European geography, 2019–2022 period, and canopy-height task remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The C1–C3 configuration comparisons and five external comparators—Liu, Tolan, Lang, Pauls, and Turubanova—are retained. The new forest-type comparison uses the same five methods; the new band and seasonal variants serve as ablation controls.

E3.justification: V2 removes RMSE from the reported metric set; Table 4 instead displays R² values already reported in Figure 5. Added protocols include equal four-month seasonal inputs with identical training-label counts, height-threshold and forest-type subsets, and an above-8-m to below-5-m potential-deforestation criterion. The original training budgets and main validation setup remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially extends analysis beyond the retained configuration comparisons and qualitative examples. Appendix B tests B01/B09 inclusion, visualizes monthly activations, compares forest types, and controls input volume when testing seasonal diversity. Appendix C adds quantitative analysis of potential deforestation between successive years.

E5.justification: Tables 6 and 8 newly report values with ± quantities, whereas the original distribution plots and Table 5's stated year-to-year standard deviation are retained. V2 does not define these new uncertainty quantities or provide run counts and seeds, so increased replication cannot be established.

E6.justification: Substantial supplementary findings are added: negligible B01/B09 effects, broadleaf/coniferous MAEs of 4.57/4.11 m for Ours, seasonal Huber losses of 1.169, 1.130, and 1.122 for winter, summer, and mixed inputs, and potential-deforestation areas of 9747.9, 7729.1, and 15942.5 km² for successive year pairs. The main MAE/MSE results remain unchanged, including Ours at 4.76 m MAE in 2020. RMSE entries disappear; Table 4's R² entries reproduce Figure 5's existing R²_7 values.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces theoretical results or proofs. The retained tensor notation and metric explanations are substantively unchanged; the new appendix thresholds are experimental selection rules rather than new mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The third numbered contribution drops its explicit attribution of performance gains to seasonal patterns and geolocation shifts. This is a limited narrowing of that statement: the main temporal-map and accuracy claims remain, and the conclusion still asserts those mechanisms.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 replaces categorical mechanism statements with potential seasonal information use and possible exploitation of geolocation offsets. Appendix B suggests B01/B09 could be removed and explicitly treats location-dependent temporal processing as a hypothesis needing confirmation. The earlier limitation concerning detection of slow tree growth is retained.

D1.justification: V2 newly discloses approximately 0.15% labeled pixels per patch and mentions forest-mask filtering. It also changes the printed Earth Engine viewer endpoint. These are documentation/access changes; the optimization settings and Appendix A data-handling procedure remain substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations including Loo and Wang (2024), Fayad et al. (2025), Tarasiou et al. (2023), and references supporting optimization, activation analysis, and forest-type data. The background now acknowledges general satellite time-series processing, while the main research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained, with local shortening, clarified wording, bulleted baseline descriptions, and publication/acknowledgement edits. New appendix narratives are inserted as B and C, moving Additional Figures from B to D without extensively reorganizing the existing argument.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 6–8 and the monthly-activation Figure 7, removes Table 2's RMSE column, and replaces Table 4's RMSE column with R². Existing displays are rearranged within the retained layout. V1 Figures 7–8 become V2 Figures 8–9; the Europe overview also receives a simplified color palette.

improvement.justification: The equal-volume seasonal ablation addresses a confound in v1's stack-versus-composite comparison, while band and forest-type analyses strengthen support for existing design choices. More cautious mechanism language also improves calibration. These gains are limited by undefined ± quantities and missing run information; the added deforestation estimates remain model-derived observations without independent validation.
